_note: Regional character, applied on top of a city's style mix. A city names its region in tools/cities.ts, which is baked into the package; anything a region leaves out comes from 'default'. Palettes replace a style's own palettes (styles.json) for that region; each palette is { wall, trim, roof, accent }.

default.note: What a North American downtown looks like: lamp posts along every pavement, benches here and there, zebra crossings at junctions.

park._note: Open country, selected by AREA rather than by city (city/park-area.ts): a tile whose park or wood polygon covers at least a quarter of it is drawn by these rules instead of the street's. The defaults INVERT here — no pavements, no furniture but a lamppost, one narrow strip of road — because a big park was built to read as countryside and every city default fights that. Shared by every city, which is the point: Golden Gate Park, the Presidio, Central Park and the Bois de Boulogne take the same rule.
park._furnitureNote: The kinds actually baked inside Golden Gate Park are stop, busstop, hydrant, food, fountain and signals - there is no mapped `lamp`. A park lamppost is PROCEDURAL, placed along a kerb by region.furniture.lampPosts and driven by `walk`, so zeroing `walk` here took the park's lampposts away with the pavements. DONE 2026-09-25: the park now has a planting of its own in render/city.ts - one side, every ~70 m, out on the verge, and not on a through-route.
park._stopNote: `stop` was added 2026-09-25 AGAINST the rule written the night before, because a photograph disagreed with it. Mapillary frame 174022498724513, on MLK Drive East at 37.76769 -122.47958, has a red STOP sign and a small green street-name blade at the junction - in a park whose standing instruction is `there are almost no signs`. Both things are true: there is almost nothing along the RUNS, and a junction where two park drives meet is signed like any other, because a driver has to be told to stop. Suppressing it does not make the park more rural, it makes the junction unreadable. The name BLADES stay suppressed, which is the owner's explicit call rather than the photograph's - see BUGS.md.
park._fogNote: The city's daylight look ships 0.0026 (render/facade-material.ts); 0.006 is 2.3x that, half-faded at about 115 m, which is where the road disappears into trunks in ~/Downloads/ggp-rural-road.png. Measured against the shipped value rather than guessed at in the abstract. 2026-10-02, owner: "i don't love the fog effect in parks. it seems to apply to buildings and ground, but not trees and cars. maybe we should tone it down" - the trees, cars and people keep the city's fog, so the thicker park air made them stand out of it; now 0.0032, a touch over the city's.

paris.note: Paris. Cream limestone almost everywhere (Haussmann's city is one colour, and that colour is what makes it Paris), slate-blue zinc roofs and black ironwork. No lamp posts on the pavement edge: Paris street lamps hang from the buildings. Black bollards (potelets) line the narrow pavements to keep cars off them. Crossings are the passage piéton: broad white bands, wider apart than a zebra (crossings: bands).

new-york.note: Brooklyn and Manhattan brownstone and walk-up country: four or five storeys, set by the row either side. Only the height method is set here so far; the rest of the New York profile is item G.

chicago.note: The Loop: towers stand beside three-storey survivors, and the towers are the ones mappers tag. The median of the tagged neighbours would make every untagged walk-up a skyscraper, so the lower quartile is asked, and capped. The rest of the Chicago profile is item G.

pavedSquares.name: Embarcadero Plaza (owner, 2026-10-04: brick, like Market's sidewalks; OSM maps it as a park)

footBridgeLayers.name: Market Street overpass and its spiral ramp, at Clayton/Corbett (Mapillary: one deck ~5 m over the road)

san-francisco.note: Nob Hill: houses and small apartment blocks, with a few hotels on the crest. The building type decides first and the neighbours are asked over a shorter distance, because a hotel tower on the corner says nothing about the Victorians down the hill. The rest of the profile is item G.

streetPaint.note: the streetcar lanes red, Gough to 3rd (owner)
